reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, wide-packet re-review batch 6, 2026-08-01

samples_reviewed.question_text: Daniel wants to cover a rectangular garden that is 22 cm long and 5 cm wide with square tiles. How many tiles are needed to cover it completely?
Kuya Bien wants to cover a rectangular garden that is 3 cm long and 11 cm wide with square tiles. How many tiles are needed to cover it completely?
Lara wants to cover a rectangular garden that is 15 cm long and 18 cm wide with square tiles. How many tiles are needed to cover it completely?
Coach Roel wants to cover a rectangular garden that is 10 cm long and 15 cm wide with square tiles. How many tiles are needed to cover it completely?
Ate Cara wants to cover a rectangular garden that is 4 cm long and 14 cm wide with square tiles. How many tiles are needed to cover it completely?
Mia wants to cover a rectangular garden that is 17 cm long and 10 cm wide with square tiles. How many tiles are needed to cover it completely?
Look at the 4×8 array. How many squares are shaded in all?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Six of seven samples pose genuine word problems with named characters solving for tile counts, e.g. seed 43's 'Kuya Bien wants to cover a rectangular garden that is 3 cm long and 11 cm wide with square tiles', matching 'solve problems involving areas' well.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The competency covers 'squares AND rectangles', but all six word problems use unequal length/width pairs (22&5, 3&11, 15&18, 10&15, 4&14, 17&10), so a square garden is never posed; seed 55's 'Look at the 4×8 array...' is also a non-square, non-word-problem duplicate of the earlier area node's content.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Single-step length-times-width garden-tiling word problems with familiar Filipino names such as Daniel, Kuya Bien, and Mia fit grade-3 quarter-1 problem-solving demand well.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Every one of the six word problems reuses the identical '[Name] wants to cover a rectangular garden that is X cm long and Y cm wide with square tiles' scenario; only the character name and dimensions change, with no alternate object such as a wall or a mat ever appearing.

competency_alignment.rationale: The dimension variation across the six garden problems, from 3x11 up to 22x5, directly builds the area-problem-solving skill this node targets.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Side lengths stay within 3-22 cm for every sample, never scaling up to a meter-based real-world area despite 'garden' being an object more naturally measured in meters.
